newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila denies fungus contamination on coconuts.
newsitem.headline: Manila denies fungus contamination on coconuts.

text.p: Philippine coconut exports to Brazil have not been contaminated with fungus, the administrator of the state agency Philippine Coconut Authority (PCA) said on Friday.

"For the record, there have not been any complaints of fungi contamination from anywhere in the world except from the Brazilian government," PCA administrator Virgilio David said in a letter to Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero, a copy of which was given to reporters.
"Even the private coconut importers of Brazil have not made any complaint," he added.
Brazil complained late last year of fungi contamination on Philippine coconut products to the Philippine embassy, David said at a news conference.

"We strongly believe that the unfounded contamination report is, to say the least, a non-tariff barrier imposition on top of the Brazilian duty of 121.5 percent on Philippine dessicated coconuts," David said.
The Philippines lodged a complaint with the World Trade Organisation on the high duty imposed by Brazil on Philippine coconut exports, he added.
David did not specify the volume of coconut products exported by the Philippines yearly to Brazil.
He said the Philippines should take measures to fight back the "barrier" imposed by Brazil on coconut products.
The trade and agriculture departments should study a counter-measure like imposing similar level of tariff on Brazilian goods entering the Philippine market, he said.
"This might be the only way to remedy the Brazilian problem," David said.
